title: kevin-zhou-private-deploy-scratchpad-2026-03-04.json
content:
Daily scratchpad / field notes for ACME private deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway) - quick reminders and blockers.

High-level summary:
- Customer: ACME Corp (finance vertical) - hybrid: VPC peering into their prod VPC + on-prem GPU hosts for inference.
- Goal this week: finish final network validation and KMS integration, deploy Control Plane v0.9.3 to their management cluster, and validate model serving on one on-prem node.

Yesterday (quick):
- Provisioned bastion in customer VPC, confirmed SSH to mgmt-jump (10.42.5.12) via SSM tunnel.
- Applied initial iptables rules on on-prem node (gpu-01) to restrict outbound to monitoring endpoints.
- Raised Jira JIRA-7892 for KMS key access timeout observed (stack traces attached).

Open blockers / notes to resolve:
1) KMS handshake failures intermittently during key unwrap (seen in control-plane logs).
   - Symptom: control-plane pod (redwood-ctrl-0) fails with "kms: unwrap timeout" ~ every 10-15m for ~30s.
   - Hypothesis: customer KMS backend throttles on bursts; our retry policy too aggressive.
   - Action items: ask infra to patch operator to backoff with jitter (increase initial backoff to 1s, max 20s). Add circuit breaker around KMS calls.
   - Temp workaround: switch to customer-provided ephemeral key for deployments (requires on-call approval).

2) Firewall / routing: Packet loss to S3-compatible object store when larger uploads (>10MB) - likely MTU mismatch on peering link.
   - Steps taken: captured tcpdump on bastion (see linked artifact CONFLUENCE-ACME-VPC-SETUP > network-logs).
   - Next: coordinate with ACME network team to verify MTU on aws-eni and their router. Try forcing MTU 1400 on tunnel as test.

Install / validation checklist (progress updated inline):
- Pre-reqs (customer):
  - [x] VPC peering and routes configured (route table IDs confirmed).
  - [x] Service account + IAM role created (ACME-Redwood-deploy) - minimal privileges granted for now.
  - [ ] KMS key policy updated to allow control plane principal (pending) - blocked by firewall/KMS timeouts.
- Control plane deploy:
  - [x] kubeconfig loaded on mgmt cluster (context: acme-mgmt-prod).
  - [x] Helm repo updated to revision containing v0.9.3 chart (chart digest: sha256:...).
  - helm install command used: helm upgrade --install redwood-control redwood/control-plane -f values-acme.yaml --namespace redwood --create-namespace
  - [ ] Confirm pod readiness for redwood-ctrl (currently CrashLoopBackOff due to KMS unwrap).
- On-prem GPU node prep (gpu-01):
  - [x] OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (kernel 5.15)
  - [x] NVIDIA driver: 535.54 installed
  - [x] CUDA runtime: 12.1 verified
  - [x] container runtime: containerd 1.7.1 (checked).
  - [ ] nvml metrics intermittently missing - need to confirm nvidia-container-toolkit config.
  - install notes: sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit; systemctl restart containerd
- Model serving smoke test:
  - [ ] Deploy test model (gpt-small-quant) to on-prem node with nodeSelector gpu=true
  - [ ] Run simple generation (prompt: "Hello, world") - check latency and logits consistency with hosted baseline.

Helpful commands / snippets (keep in scratchpad):
- Check control plane logs:
  kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=redwood-control --since=30m
- Describe failing pod:
  kubectl -n redwood describe pod redwood-ctrl-0
- Port-forward to controller for local debugging:
  kubectl -n redwood port-forward svc/redwood-control 8080:8080
- KMS debug env (temporary): set REDWOOD_KMS_DEBUG=1 in pod env and restart

Customer env reminders / gotchas:
- ACME uses a private S3-compatible object store (Ceph RGW) with IAM compatibility layer - requires sigv4 header handling; some SDKs need explicit region header.
- Their firewall blocks outbound on non-standard ports; ensure all endpoints (metrics, object store, KMS) are allowed.
- HSM: they have a network HSM in a separate rack; latency to HSM can spike during backups - schedule heavy jobs outside backup windows (customer backup window 02:00-03:00 local).
- Their ops team prefers rolling restarts during morning hours 09:00-11:00 PST. Avoid changes outside that window without explicit approval.

Short-term plan (next 48h):
- Today: collect more KMS logs, bump control-plane backoff, and deploy a canary that switches to SDK client with longer timeouts. (owner: Maya)
- Tomorrow: try MTU 1400 on bastion tunnel and re-run large upload test to object store (owner: Kevin).
- If KMS problem persists: prepare a fallback to local PEM-encrypted key for model metadata (security review required).

To-dos (personal):
- [ ] Write up short internal note summarizing KMS failure patterns and proposed retry fix (link to PR).
- [x] Ping ACME network lead (Tom L.) about MTU measurements (he confirmed he can test later today).
- [ ] Add automated metric for KMS unwrap latency to control-plane dashboard (create ticket).
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with customer ops for Friday to go over restart windows and HSM backup schedule.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep sample payloads small when debugging KMS (smaller calls less likely to trigger throttle).
- Remember to redact IPs and ARNs when sharing screenshots in Confluence.

End of scratchpad for 2026-03-04.
